newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton upbeat on Christmas potential.
newsitem.headline: Ashton upbeat on Christmas potential.

text.p: Argyle diamond mine partner Ashton Mining Ltd said on Monday there were "good signs" for worldwide diamond demand during the 1996 Christmas period.
"The indications are that the Christmas retail period is, in an international sense..., beginning to show good signs," Ashton chief executive John Robinson told a media briefing.
Demand indicators in the U.S. also boded well for the growing Indian diamond market over Christmas, he added.
"The feel-good factor in the U.S. is continuing and, as far as the Indian business is concerned, it's the U.S. Christmas period that's the key," he said.
Robinson said the decision to cut ties with De Beers' Central Selling Organisation (CSO) in June had been vindicated by sales during the second and third quarters of calendar 1996.
"The trends that are evident so far are very encouraging. We've exceeded the forecast we set ourselves at the beginning of the six-month period," he said.
Robinson decline to elaborate on what the company's forecasts were.
Robinson said output from the Merlin diamond project in the Northern Territory would improve the company's product range and make it more attractive for the Indian market.

"In terms of perception it's very important because what it does provide Ashton with is a broader range of product. It takes us into the mainstream and the larger proportion of that material could be cut and polished in India," he said.
Ashton, a 32.93 percent partner in the project, last week made a A$1.40 a share mop-up bid for 70 percent-owned unit Australian Diamond Exploration NL which in turn owns 44.5 percent of Merlin.
